definitions.explanation: addressing the root cause of a problem rather than just the symptoms; fundamental reform or change

examples.japanese: {抜本的|ばっぽんてき}な{改革|かいかく}が{必要|ひつよう}だ。
{問題|もんだい}を{抜本的|ばっぽんてき}に{解決|かいけつ}する。
examples.english: To solve the problem radically/at its root.

examples.japanese: {制度|せいど}の{抜本的|ばっぽんてき}な{見直|みなお}しが{求|もと}められている。
examples.english: A fundamental review of the system is being called for.

notes:
{抜本|ばっぽん} means addressing something at its root or fundamentally.

COMPOSITION:
- {抜|ばつ}: To pull out, extract
- {本|ぽん}: Root, origin

Literal meaning: "pulling out the root" - addressing the fundamental cause.

MOST COMMON FORM:
Usually appears as {抜本的|ばっぽんてき} (na-adjective form).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {抜本的|ばっぽんてき}な{改革|かいかく} (fundamental reform)
- {抜本的|ばっぽんてき}な{対策|たいさく} (drastic measures)
- {抜本的|ばっぽんてき}な{見直|みなお}し (fundamental review)
- {抜本的|ばっぽんてき}に{解決|かいけつ}する (to solve radically)
- {抜本的|ばっぽんてき}な{変革|へんかく} (fundamental transformation)

CONTRAST:
- {抜本的|ばっぽんてき} (fundamental - addresses root cause)
- {対症|たいしょう}{療法|りょうほう}{的|てき} (symptomatic - only addresses symptoms)

RELATED TERMS:
- {根本的|こんぽんてき} (fundamental - similar meaning)
- {抜本塞源|ばっぽんそくげん} (to uproot completely - idiom)

REGISTER: Formal. Common in news, politics, and business contexts.
